To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) default rules can be viewed as non-deter- ministic generators of partial models; (ii) a natural generalization of the standard class of semi-normal default rule sets is obtained by replacing the condition of normality with the condition of rationality; (iii) the existence of dilations for rational default rule sets is proved, thus improving the standard theory of default logic; (iv) the theory of rational default rule sets can be extended to the theory of rational information structures,

(a) the class of rational default information structures is the largest class of such structures for which the existence of dilations is guaranteed, (b) this class includes, but is strictly larger than, the class of semi-normal default rule systems, and (c) the existence of dilated models for a rational structure S implies that S has a canonical dilation, which is the unique dilation for which the set of dilated models is closed under intersection.
(i) the class of rational default information structures is robust and (ii) the class of dilations of such rational structures is non-empty

the class of rational default information structures is a robust generalisation of the class of Reiter's default rule systems, which is a robust generalisatio n of the class of propositional default rule systems, and which is a robust specialisation of the class o f default information structures.

the class of rational default information structures is a proper generalization of the class of semi-normal default information structures, and that the latter class, in turn, is a proper generaliza- tion of the class of standard default rule systems.
we have developed the theory of a new kind of default logic, based on domain theory, which is more general and more powerful than the original Reiter's one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a general framework for the study of default logic, and we provide a new, natural and robust class of default information structure, with a clear and simple semantics, which includes the class of semi-normal default theories.
, in the framework of domain theory, we provide a new semantics for default logic, based on a new notion of dilation.
we have shown that default logic is a natural and robust extension of classical first order logic, and that domain theory provides a useful framework for its study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard de nitions of extensions and preferred extensions are not adequate for default information structures.
the domain-theoretical perspective provides a natural way to view the semantics of default information structures.
the theory of default logic can be seen as an instance of domain theory, in a way that is faithful to the original intuitions of the subject.
